10.question: When you talk about educational equality, what do you focus on most?

options.label: Applying the same rules everywhere.
The differences between schools serving different social classes.
Whether students enjoy the learning process.
Whether educational methods can keep evolving in real situations.

11.question: If you clearly saw a pig flying through the sky, what would you think?

options.label: This breed of pig must naturally be able to fly.
That is not a pig; it must be another animal.
I may have seen it wrong—or I may have food poisoning.
Perhaps pigs can fly; perhaps we were wrong before.

12.question: Which statement comes closest to your view of what truly exists?

options.label: What exists is what can be measured and repeatedly verified.
What matters most is the relationship between beings, not beings in isolation.
Existence depends on consciousness paying attention; what nobody notices has little significance.
Existence and its relations are an ongoing process of becoming; at first, there was nothing.

13.question: You are assembling furniture and the instructions seem to contain a mistake. What is your first reaction?

options.label: Follow the steps; success is bound to come.
The problem must be entirely with the person who made it.
My understanding may differ from the maker's intention.
Start doing it and figure things out as I go.

14.question: When you see controversial news, what do you think?

options.label: Even if the issue is complicated, looking at it from several angles will reveal the truth.
There always seems to be some hidden force operating behind the scenes.
Different perspectives reveal different truths.
Even if the truth is unknown, what matters is knowing how the visible problem was resolved.

15.question: When you see controversial news, where are you most likely to find the problem?

options.label: Start with the official announcement.
Start with facts that can be established and checked.
Judge it from my past experience.
Start with contradictions in the news report.

16.question: What do you think the “filter” in romantic love is?

options.label: A normal biological response caused by dopamine in the brain.
Using illusion to push back against the mediocrity of reality.
The fact that we can never truly know another person.
Because I love them, they shine.

17.question: You and a friend understand the same event in completely different ways. What is your first reaction?

options.label: One of us must have misunderstood the facts.
We are each standing in a different position.
Everyone naturally sees things differently.
Perhaps the event itself has no fixed form.
A team where nobody has ever made a mistake and I only need to play my assigned role.
A team led by an outstanding leader.
A team in which every individual can influence the whole.
A team that inevitably has problems, but where everyone is willing to reflect.

02.question: A city wants to tackle traffic congestion. Which of these do you think is the best place to start?

options.label: Existing theory matters most, so we should follow the experts' recommendations exactly.
Have the construction companies and experts discuss the issue and agree on a solution.
Involve residents too, discuss it together, and settle on a plan.
Try a small-scale solution first, then discuss the results and adjust it with everyone.

03.question: Your country announces a goal of overtaking the United States in AI within a year. How do you feel about it?

options.label: The United States is too powerful, so there is no chance of that happening.
It is just a contest between grand forces, and it has little to do with me.
Could such an aggressive strategy end up oppressing individuals?
Breaking a hegemony matters, and no attempt is a genuine failure.

04.question: What do you think about the nature of natural laws—for example, the fact that the sun rises in the east?

options.label: Natural laws are the essence of the world; we only need to discover and use them.
Some higher power governs these laws from behind the scenes.
Natural laws are only products of human understanding; the real world may not be this way.
Natural laws are shared habits of experience, and they may be overturned in the future.

05.question: As an ordinary person, which of the following seems like the better course of action?

options.label: Quickly overthrow the bourgeoisie and establish a society fully ruled by the proletariat.
Because real-world struggle is so harsh, online attacks on the bourgeoisie are the key tactic for now.
Become a capitalist, accumulate capital, and only then gain the power to overthrow the bourgeoisie.
Take responsibility in the real world while helping and supporting the workers around you.

06.question: As a modern person, how do you view Confucian culture?

options.label: Half of the Analects is enough to govern the empire.
Study it in ways that respond to my actual needs.
An outdated philosophy that constrains human freedom.
An old order that must be completely shattered.

07.question: When it comes to human death, which view do you agree with most?

options.label: Death is the end of a human being as a living part of nature.
The death of working people is a liberation and elevation of life.
The certainty of death forces us to ask what it means to be alive.
The meaning of an individual's death can be rewritten by the future.

08.question: Which situation best expresses your sense of self?

options.label: When I become someone admired by society's shared values.
When I resist society's shared values.
When I am happy.
There is no single self; different situations bring out different selves.

09.question: What do you think is the essence of history?

options.label: A process of change with patterns we can recognize.
A bloody history of one power replacing another.
A narrative woven by outstanding individuals.
A little girl anyone can dress up.
